title: Marked identity-reducing automorphism subgroup of a dual-number thickening
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $p_i:S\to X$ for $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, where $n\geq0$, be specified morphisms (in applications sections). Let $X[\epsilon]$ be the constant dual-number thickening with the same underlying space as $X$ and structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O_X$, $\epsilon^2=0$ [def-sc-dual-numbers]; define $S[\epsilon]$ similarly, and let $f[\epsilon]:X[\epsilon]\to S[\epsilon]$ and $p_i[\epsilon]:S[\epsilon]\to X[\epsilon]$ be the induced maps. The marked infinitesimal automorphism group $A(f,p)$ is the subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}_{S[\epsilon]}(X[\epsilon])$ consisting of $\alpha$ such that $\alpha\circ\iota_X=\iota_X$ for the closed immersion $\iota_X:X\to X[\epsilon]$ setting $\epsilon=0$, and $\alpha\circ p_i[\epsilon]=p_i[\epsilon]$ for every $i$. It is the intersection of the corresponding postcomposition stabilizers, pulled back from scheme automorphisms to automorphisms over $S[\epsilon]$. For $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, the canonical isomorphism $S[\epsilon]\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{DualNumber}k)$ identifies this with the usual base-changed thickening over the dual numbers. Empty markings impose no extra condition.
